On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

name: reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes
description: "A failing test with a fake backend is not a reproduction; run the pre-fix code against the real thing before fixing, and say what was and was not seen"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A failing Catch2 test with a fake backend proves the code does what the brief says, not that the bug is real. Before fixing, run the code from before the fix against the real thing, with what the app actually knows printed beside what it says.

**Why:** on 2026-11-01 Kenneth asked whether I had reproduced three printer chat bugs, and I had only fakes for them: "I don't want you to fix the bugs that are in imagination only". The real run then showed one was only partly real as briefed: the "No printer in LAN mode" sentence was true of a printer in cloud mode.

**How to apply:** do it before writing the fix. To do it afterwards, swap production files with `git show <base>:<file>`, keep a temporary harness script, rebuild, and restore from `git show HEAD:<file>`. In zsh, loop over an array: a plain string variable does not split. Run harnesses with cwd in the scratchpad: the Bambu plug-in writes `log_iotc.txt` into the cwd. See [[printer-network-check-harness]].

name: manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe
description: "Reproduce any JusPrin tool behaviour without a live model in about 20 s per run: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py call(); two traps (leaked harness from `cd && cmd &`, slice_start on an unchanged sliced plate)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 0b03c379-ea3d-491e-a0b3-9b5bf2a6240f
  modified: 2026-10-12T23:51:00.507Z
---

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

input.recap: The fix for GitHub issue 39 is on branch claude/nozzle-sizes-comma-locale: nozzle and bed sizes now read correctly when the app runs in Portuguese, German, French and similar languages. Unit tests and the include check pass. Nothing is committed, and it is not yet checked by clicking through the real app.
input.ask: May I take over the screen for a few minutes to check the fix in the real app?

content.text:
The reporter's problem is a JusPrin bug, and it affects far more than this one printer. Their 0.4 mm profile ships in 2.0.0, but when JusPrin runs in a language that writes decimals with a comma (Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and others), the add-printer form finds no nozzle sizes for almost any printer. The reporter writes "0,4", so their app is almost certainly running in one of those languages.

**The cause.** When the app starts in Portuguese, wxWidgets switches the C library's number format to Portuguese. JusPrin's own add-printer code reads the sizes in the printer profiles with `std::stod`, which follows that format. So it reads "0.4" as 0, and the Creator 5 Pro ends up with no sizes at all. The AI then tells the person it doesn't support 0.4 mm, which matches the issue. I checked this by compiling the real catalog code and running it against the real profiles:

- **C or English number format:** the Creator 5 Pro gets 0.25, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm, and 0 of 454 printer models lose their sizes.
- **Portuguese number format:** the Creator 5 Pro gets no sizes, and 412 of 454 models lose theirs.

The same mistake cuts fractional bed sizes short (one printer's 233.5 mm width reads as 233). It also reads a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF as 0, and tells the AI about a nozzle mismatch as "0,2" instead of "0.2".

**The fix.** It's in a new worktree at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/nozzle-sizes-comma-locale`, on branch `claude/nozzle-sizes-comma-locale`, starting from `jusprin-dev`. Four places now parse numbers with OrcaSlicer's existing `string_to_double_decimal_point` and `atof_decimal_point`, which read "0.4" the same in every language. The nozzle-mismatch text is now written by the JSON library instead of `snprintf`. All the changed code is JusPrin's own; no OrcaSlicer-owned file changed.

**Tests.** I added three tests that switch the number format to Portuguese:
- The Creator 5 Pro and every other printer keep their nozzle sizes, and the 233.5 mm bed stays 233.5.
- A file's nozzle size still reads as 0.4 and 0.6.
- The nozzle-mismatch text still says "0.2" and "0.4".

Each one failed on the old code and passes with the fix. Both full test suites pass: 180 JusPrin test cases and 581 agent test cases. The include check that CI runs passes on all changed files.

**Still open:**
- **The real-app check.** I launched the installed 2.0.0 in Portuguese and got to the "Which printer do you have?" screen. But choosing Flashforge in the Brand menu needs full-screen control, and the approval prompt timed out twice, so neither the broken screen nor the fixed one has been seen in the app yet. The fixed build is ready at `build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app` in the worktree.
- **Nothing is committed**, and I haven't replied on the issue. Here's a reply you could post:

> Thanks for the report. This is a bug in JusPrin 2.0.0: when the app runs in a language that writes decimals with a comma, such as Portuguese, the printer list loses its nozzle sizes. The fix will be in the next release. Until then, switching JusPrin's language to English in Preferences should let you add the Creator 5 Pro with the 0.4 mm nozzle.

The English workaround in that reply follows from the cause, but I haven't tried it in the app.
Yes, take the screen

content.text:
I reproduced the bug in the installed JusPrin 2.0.0, and my fixed build fixes it. With the app in Portuguese, 2.0.0 shows the Creator 5 Pro's nozzle row as " mm, the only size it comes with" with no number, and Continue stays greyed out. The fixed build shows 0,25 / 0,4 / 0,6 / 0,8 mm with 0,4 selected. Pressing Continue added the printer with the "Flashforge Creator 5 Pro 0.4 nozzle" profile. I sent you both screenshots; they're in `.claude/issue-39-shots/` in the worktree and stay untracked.

**Why the first check on the Mac looked fine.** My first attempt with the installed 2.0.0 showed the nozzle buttons, so the bug didn't appear. With the debugger I found the reason:
- At startup, wxWidgets sets the app's number format to Portuguese, where "0.4" reads as 0.
- When the app is opened from Finder it has no `LANG` setting. The bundled Python then resets the whole number format to "C" a moment later, which hides the bug.
- When I started the same app with `LANG` set (as a terminal or a Linux desktop provides), the format stayed Portuguese. The running app's C library then read "0.4" as 0, and the form lost every nozzle size.

**Effect on the reporter.** Python's documentation lists this reset (its "C locale coercion") as Unix-only, so it never runs on Windows. That means the reporter's Windows copy keeps the Portuguese number format and hits the bug every time. I haven't run it on Windows itself; this rests on the Python documentation plus the Mac result with `LANG` set. Linux users with a comma-decimal language would normally hit it too, because their desktop sets `LANG`.

**The fix.** It's on branch `claude/nozzle-sizes-comma-locale` in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/nozzle-sizes-comma-locale`, unchanged from my last message:
- JusPrin's own code now reads sizes from profiles and files with OrcaSlicer's locale-independent parsers instead of `std::stod`.
- The nozzle-mismatch text sent to the AI is written by the JSON library instead of `snprintf`.
- The three new tests fail without the fix and pass with it. Both full test suites and the include check pass.

**Still open:**
- **Nothing is committed**, and I haven't replied on GitHub. The reply I drafted last time still stands. Its English-language workaround follows from this finding but I haven't tried it, so I'd drop it if you want to post only what's confirmed.
- **A small display difference I didn't change.** In the fixed build, the printer card on Home shows "0.4 mm" while the printer form shows "0,4 mm". That's how the existing code writes sizes, and I didn't look into it.
commit it and post the reply on the issue.

cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/nozzle-sizes-comma-locale; git add src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolResults.cpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterCatalog.cpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/LoadFacts.cpp tests/agent/CMakeLists.txt tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp tests/jusprin/CMakeLists.txt tests/jusprin/test_load_facts.cpp tests/jusprin/test_printer_catalog.cpp tests/jusprin_support/CommaLocale.hpp; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Read printer sizes the same in every language

When JusPrin runs in a language that writes decimals with a comma
(Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and others), the add-printer
form showed no nozzle sizes for almost every printer, so the printer could
not be added. GitHub issue TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#39 reports it for
the Flashforge Creator 5 Pro and its 0.4 mm nozzle.

wxWidgets sets the C library's number format to the app's language at
startup. JusPrin's printer catalog read the sizes in the printer profiles
with std::stod, which follows that format, so "0.4" read as 0. With the
number format set to Portuguese, 412 of 454 printer models lost their
nozzle sizes, and fractional bed sizes were cut short (233.5 mm read as
233). The same mistake read a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF as 0, and
told the AI about a nozzle mismatch as "0,2" instead of "0.2".

On macOS the bug is usually hidden: an app opened from Finder has no LANG
setting, and the bundled Python's startup then resets the whole C locale
to "C". Python does this only on Unix, so Windows always shows the bug.

The catalog, the printer backend and the 3MF facts now parse with
OrcaSlicer's locale-independent string_to_double_decimal_point and
atof_decimal_point. The mismatch text is written by the JSON library
instead of snprintf. The test programs compile LocalesUtils.cpp directly,
as they do the JusPrin sources they test.

Tested: three new tests switch the number format to Portuguese; each fails
without this change and passes with it. jusprin_tests (180 cases) and
agent_bridge_tests (581 cases) pass, and the clang-tidy include check
passes on the changed lines. In the real app on macOS, started with LANG
set and the language set to Portuguese, JusPrin 2.0.0 showed no nozzle
size for the Creator 5 Pro and kept Continue disabled; this build showed
0.25, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm and added the printer with its 0.4 mm profile.
Not run on Windows.
EOF

=================== #37
[Bug][Linux] Plate analysis sends empty images: wx JPEG save fails ("JPEG: Couldnt save image")
by samuk10 2026-10-07T22:57:33Z
labels: []

### Summary

When the AI panel renders the plate views for analysis, `JusPrinPlateUtils::RenderPlateView` encodes each of the 4 views as **JPEG**:

```cpp
std::string base64_image = encode_thumbnail_to_base64(data, false); // true for PNG, false for JPEG
```

On Linux builds, `wxImage::SaveFile(stream, wxBITMAP_TYPE_JPEG)` fails silently. The client log shows exactly 4 failures per analysis:

```
[warning] Error: JPEG: Couldn't save image.   (x4, one per view)
```

`encode_thumbnail_to_base64` then still prepends the data URI prefix, producing `data:image/jpeg;base64,` with an **empty payload**. That string is truthy, so it passes the frontend filter (`renderResult.filter(result => result.base64)`) and reaches the server, where the provider rejects the whole request and the chat shows a generic "an error occurred" message. Plate analysis is effectively broken on Linux.

### Fix

---
name: macos-finder-launch-hides-locale-bugs
description: "On macOS an app opened from Finder/open has no LANG, so the bundled Python resets LC_ALL to C and hides comma-decimal locale bugs; launch with open --env LANG=en_US.UTF-8 to see what Windows users get"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Found 2026-11-16 while reproducing GitHub issue 39 (Creator 5 Pro had no nozzle sizes in Portuguese; fixed in d010a88c1a by parsing with Orca's `string_to_double_decimal_point`).

wxLocale::Init sets LC_ALL to the app language (e.g. "pt_BR"), so `std::stod`/`strtod`/`snprintf` use a comma. But when the app is started by Finder or plain `open`, the process has no `LANG`, and the bundled Python's startup (`_Py_CoerceLegacyLocale`, C locale coercion) calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")`, which resets every category to "C". The bug then vanishes on the Mac. Python documents this coercion as Unix-only, so Windows keeps the comma format; Linux desktops set LANG, so they keep it too.

**How to apply:** to reproduce a locale bug on the Mac, set the language in the scratch conf (`{"app":{"language":"pt_BR"}}`) and launch with `open -n --env LANG=en_US.UTF-8 <app> --args --datadir <scratch>`. Confirm with `lldb -p <pid> --batch -o 'expr (const char*)setlocale(0,(const char*)0)'` (expect "pt_BR/..."). A Finder launch that looks fine is not evidence the bug is absent. Related: [[reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

I didn't find the exact audit message "GitHub fork (not canonical repository)" in the results. The closest material is Homebrew's policy on forks, which explains why a fork can be flagged.

- **Forks normally stay out of the main cask repo.** Homebrew's guidance says stable versions live in the main repository at Homebrew/homebrew-cask.
- **Forks can replace the original only in limited cases.** Per the current docs, a fork may replace the original cask when it meets the shared fork criteria. A cask-specific exception also exists when clear evidence shows that the fork is so overwhelmingly adopted that users understand the original name to mean the fork.
- **Official successor status counts.** One listed criterion is that the fork has been designated the official successor in the original source repository (e.g. in the README) or in a publicly verifiable way by the original author.
- **The alternative is a separate cask.** An alternative to the fork replacing the original cask is a new cask.
- **Popularity thresholds apply.** Rejected casks include an app from a code repository that is not notable enough (under 30 forks, 30 watchers, 75 stars).

The likely explanation is that the audit flags a cask whose URL or source points to a fork rather than the canonical Homebrew/homebrew-cask project. The search didn't confirm the exact wording or the code path. Checking the `brew audit` source on GitHub or the Homebrew discussions forum would be the next step.

input.recap: The fixes for GitHub issues 39 and 40 and the Windows test fix are committed on jusprin-dev but not pushed; it is 8 commits ahead. The JusPrin submission to Homebrew fails Homebrew's automatic check because the JusPrin GitHub repository is marked as a fork of OrcaSlicer.
input.ask: How should JusPrin get onto Homebrew, given the fork check blocks it?

content.text:
Yes, a few things are still open. The biggest new one is that JusPrin's submission to Homebrew will fail as it stands.

**The submission to Homebrew fails.** The pull request is [Homebrew/homebrew-cask#303257](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/pull/303257). The session that wrote it reported itself done without noticing that Homebrew's test failed with "GitHub fork (not canonical repository)". I read Homebrew's source on this Mac. Its check looks at the cask's download link, and at the homepage if the link isn't on GitHub. If that repository is marked as a GitHub fork, the check fails, however many stars it has. Both of our links point to TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin, which GitHub lists as a fork of OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer. No Homebrew maintainer has commented yet.

**Decision needed: how JusPrin gets onto Homebrew.** It's your call because each fix changes something public. There are three options:
- **Run our own tap.** A tap is a small GitHub repository of install recipes. People would type `brew install thespaghettidetective/jusprin/jusprin`, and no Homebrew review is involved. It's quick and easy to undo, but harder to discover, and we would close the pull request.
- **Detach the repository from OrcaSlicer's fork network on GitHub.** The plain `brew install --cask jusprin` would then work. The repository would stop showing "forked from OrcaSlicer", and that is hard to reverse. I haven't checked whether GitHub lets you do this yourself or needs a support request.
- **Host the download and the homepage off GitHub**, for example on the JusPrin website. This changes the release workflow.

I'd pick our own tap. It gets the issue 12 reporter a working install now, and it leaves the bigger choice about the fork for later.

**Still open from the other work:**
- **Nothing is pushed.** jusprin-dev is 8 commits ahead of GitHub. They include the fix for issue 39, the fix for issue 40, the Windows test fix, and the change that makes release builds sign the Mac app by default. That default reaches GitHub's Run workflow form only after a push. One of the 8, "The app tells its server once per start that it started", came from another session. The replies on issues 39 and 40 promise the fixes in the next release, so both issues stay open until it ships.
- **Issue 40 is only tested against stand-ins.** Stand-ins are simulated printers running on the Mac. Nobody has tried a real Centauri Carbon or sent a print to any of the newly supported connection types.
- **The include check for issue 40 hasn't run.** That's the check that every changed file includes the headers it uses. It needs a newer clang-tidy than this Mac has, so it will first run in CI after the push.
- **A known weakness in issue 40.** When the chat gives up on a printer that never answers, the connection test can keep one thread busy until the printer answers or the app quits.
- **Two questions are waiting in the [Issue 40 session](#local_d4756db3-d543-4cd9-82bf-8127f6b55132).** One is whether to run the paid live test where someone plays a person stuck connecting their printer. The other is whether to update and commit the November 4 draft guide for writing connection skills.

Sources: [Homebrew Acceptable Casks](https://docs.brew.sh/Acceptable-Casks), and Homebrew's local source at `/opt/homebrew/Library/Homebrew/utils/shared_audits.rb:426` and `cask/audit.rb:1508`.
Use our own tap

input.summary: Move JusPrin's Homebrew cask to our own tap
input.message:
Kenneth chose to publish JusPrin through our own Homebrew tap. His words: "Use our own tap".

Why: your pull request Homebrew/homebrew-cask#303257 fails Homebrew's CI test with "GitHub fork (not canonical repository)". The cause is in /opt/homebrew/Library/Homebrew/utils/shared_audits.rb:426. That check fails any cask whose download link (or, failing that, its homepage) points to a GitHub repository marked as a fork, and TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer. cask/audit.rb:1508 is where the check picks which link to read.

Please do this:
1. Create the public repository TheSpaghettiDetective/homebrew-jusprin. Put the jusprin cask in Casks/jusprin.rb, plus a short README that gives the install command `brew install thespaghettidetective/jusprin/jusprin`.
2. Test it from the tap the way a user would: brew tap, brew install --cask, launch the app, then uninstall. Also run brew audit --cask --strict on it. A tap doesn't need to pass the fork or notability checks, but every other check should pass.
3. Close #303257 with a one-line comment saying JusPrin will be distributed through its own tap instead.
4. Draft a reply for GitHub issue 12 that gives the install command. Don't post it; bring the text back to Kenneth.

Commit 0e4c5063f7, which makes release builds sign and notarise the Mac app by default, should still stay. Check that its commit message doesn't claim the app is on Homebrew's main list. If it does, say so; don't amend it.

Report back with the tap's URL, the test results, and the drafted reply.
